**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — 1,132 lines.

## Problem statement

The worklist mouse-input test suite exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability
ceiling (~1,132 lines) and should be decomposed so that no test file exceeds the
ceiling.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file exceeds 1,000 lines.
2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).
3. No new circular imports.
4. All related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate test groups and update imports; do not change test
  assertions or test logic.
- **Test-file scope.** This item exists because the producer declined to include
  test-file decomposition in WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (intake Q1 → answer A):
  "production modules only; tests stay unmodified as the behaviour gate and a
  follow-up item is filed for the two oversized suites."
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B** — *Decompose packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts god class*
  (parent epic; discovered-from intake Q1 → answer A).

## Sequencing & validation (added at plan time, WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B)

- **Prerequisite:** `WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N` (finalise the production barrel) — the
  production split must land first; splitting these tests against a moving
  barrel would churn imports twice.
- **Test-first gate:** the worklist split guard
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`, `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J`)
  already asserts every production module ≤1,000 lines. Extend the same guard
  (or add a sibling guard) to assert every `worklist*.test.ts` file is ≤1,000
  lines once this item lands.
- **Move-only:** relocate describe blocks and their imports; assertions and test
  names stay byte-identical. Import from concrete `worklist.*.js` module paths
  only where the barrel does not expose an internal symbol — never from
  `index.ts`.
- **Validation:** `tsc --noEmit`/build, split guard green, and the full
  `packages/herdr` suite green (`/skill:test`).

# Refactor guard: worklist split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — must stay unchanged and green

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Precedent: `WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E` (downtime-worker split guard) — same shape,
  same AC numbering, already green on `dev`.

# Cross-repo dependencies: discover sibling project stores, resolve foreign blockers, request a clone when absent

## Goal (headline)

`wl` can **record, resolve and honour dependency edges whose target lives in
another project's store**, discovered automatically from sibling folders, so a
consumer item can be genuinely blocked by an upstream item in a different
repository instead of by a prose note that no tool enforces. When the foreign
project is not present locally, `wl` asks the producer for its git URL and
clones it.

**Created at the producer's direction (2026-10-31)** while unblocking
LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X (llm repo): that item is blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB
(SorraAgents) across stores, `wl dep add` cannot express the edge
(`Work item not found`), and `blocked` does not persist without an edge — so
the consumer's guard child reported `open` and looked startable, which would
have landed a red test. The producer chose to fix this in the tool rather than
by a placeholder item.

## Users and user stories

- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent working on a consumer item, I want the
  upstream item in another repository to block me mechanically, so I cannot
  start work whose precondition does not exist yet."
- **Producer** — "As the producer, I want the tool to discover the projects on
  this machine by itself and, when one is missing, tell me exactly what to
  clone instead of failing with `Work item not found`."
- **Framework maintainer** — "As the owner of the agent skills, I want one
  resolution rule in `wl` core so the skills stop re-implementing a
  prefix→sibling scan (there are already two copies)."

## Current behaviour (measured 2026-10-31)

| Observation | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Cross-store edges cannot be recorded | `wl dep add <local-id> <foreign-id>` → `Work item not found: <foreign-id>` (`src/commands/dep.ts` validates both endpoints against the local DB only) |
| `blocked` cannot stand in for the edge | `wl` reconciles `blocked`→`open` from the edge graph; an item with no edge cannot hold `blocked` (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` `reconcileBlockedStatus`) |
| Blocker semantics live in one predicate | `isDependencyActive()` — `status` in `completed`/`deleted` or `stage` in `in_review`/`done` is inactive; everything else blocks |
| The prefix→sibling scan already exists twice outside `wl` core | `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/work-item-title.ts` (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501) and the skills layer `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`) |
| Store discovery must not be fooled by worktrees | every implement/audit worktree checks out `.worklog/config.yaml`, so `/worktree/.worklog/` exists but holds no data — `isGenuineWorklogStore()` (`src/worklog-paths.ts`) is the existing discriminator (`initialized` or `worklog.db`) |
| Framework classifies cross-prefix edges as coordination notes only | SorraAgents `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`wl_dep_blockers`, `coordination_blockers`, SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T) |

## Required behaviour (design constraints)

**D1 — Discovery.** Scan a *projects root* (default: the parent directory of the
current checkout; overridable via config, e.g. `projectsRoot: <path>`) for
**immediate subdirectories** that hold a **genuine** local store
(`isGenuineWorklogStore`, i.e. `.worklog/initialized` or `.worklog/worklog.db` —
presence of `.worklog/` alone is NOT sufficient, because worktrees carry a
tracked `config.yaml`). Build a `prefix → <project>/.worklog` map from each
store's `config.yaml` `prefix`. Deterministic (sorted), memoised per process,
no repository-wide walk. A duplicate prefix declared by several projects is
**reported as ambiguous**, never silently picked. Non-git folders, hidden
folders and managed worktrees are excluded.

**D2 — Recording foreign edges.** `wl dep add` / `dep rm` / `dep list` accept an
id whose prefix belongs to a discovered sibling store. The foreign endpoint is
resolved **read-only** (open the sibling DB read-only; never write, never sync,
never take a mutation lock on it) purely to validate existence and to read its
title/status/stage. The edge is stored in the **local** store with the foreign
id as target, and same-project behaviour (including the automatic `blocked`
status flip) is unchanged.

**D3 — Gating on foreign targets.** Every place that evaluates dependency
blockers (`isDependencyActive` consumers: `wl next`, `wl worklist`, `wl list`,
`doctor` dependency check, `dep list`) resolves a foreign target's
`status`/`stage` from its own store using the **same** terminal semantics as
today. Fail-safe: if the foreign store is missing, unreadable, or the target
cannot be resolved, the dependent **stays blocked** and the blocker is reported
with `unresolved: true` + a reason in JSON — it never silently unblocks.

**D4 — Missing project: ask, then clone.** When a dependency id's prefix has no
discovered store, do not report a bare `Work item not found`. Emit an actionable,
machine-readable result (`success: false`, `error_code: "unknown_project"`,
`prefix`, `projects_root`, `remediation`) that asks the producer for the git URL,
plus the exact command to run:

```
wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url> [--path <projects-root>/<name>]
```

`wl project add` records the mapping in the project config, clones the
repository when the path does not exist (`git clone <url> <path>`), validates
that the cloned store's `prefix` matches, and is idempotent (re-running on an
existing correct clone is a no-op). It must **not** read stdin by default —
agents cannot answer prompts — an explicit `--interactive` may prompt for the
URL. A failed clone leaves no config mapping behind.

**D5 — Sync isolation is preserved.** The existing cross-project guards
(`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `prefix-filter.ts`) still refuse a sync that would
merge foreign-prefix items; a sibling store is never exported, imported, synced
or locked against its owner's own `wl` writes. Regression tests pin both.

**D6 — One implementation, consumers converge.** The scan lives once, in `wl`
core, exposed through a JSON surface (`wl project list --json`,
`wl dep list --json` foreign entries). The two existing copies (TUI title
resolver, skills `status_lifecycle.py`) become follow-ups that call it; the
framework change that makes the implement skill treat a **resolvable**
cross-repo edge as a real blocker (rather than a coordination note) is a
separate SorraAgents item — out of scope here, recorded in Related work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Discovery.** A test tree with several sibling projects (one with
  `tests` support, one without), a worktree-shaped stub `.worklog/` (only
  `config.yaml`), a non-git folder and two projects declaring the same prefix
  yields: only genuine stores discovered, deterministic sorted `prefix → path`
  output, duplicate prefix reported as ambiguous, and a config override of the
  projects root honoured.
- **AC2 — Foreign edge recorded, foreign store untouched.** `wl dep add` with a
  foreign id succeeds, the edge is listed by `dep list` with the foreign title
  and status, the local dependent is set to `blocked`, and the sibling DB's file
  (content hash and mtime) is unchanged. Same-project `dep add`/`rm`/`list`
  output is byte-identical to today (regression).
- **AC3 — Gating.** An item whose only active blocker is a foreign item is
  excluded from `wl next` and included with `--include-blocked`; the same item
  becomes selectable once the foreign item reaches `in_review`/`done`/
  `completed`/`deleted`; a removed sibling store leaves the item blocked with
  `unresolved: true` and a reason in JSON (never unblocked).
- **AC4 — Missing project remediation.** An unknown prefix produces
  `error_code: "unknown_project"` with the projects root and the exact
  `wl project add <PREFIX> --git-url <url>` remediation; `wl project add` clones
  into the projects root, records the mapping, validates the prefix, and is
  idempotent; a prefix mismatch or clone failure exits non-zero without leaving
  a mapping behind; no stdin prompt without `--interactive`.
- **AC5 — Sync isolation.** Existing cross-project sync guard and prefix-filter
  tests still pass, plus a new test proving a foreign store is opened read-only
  (no write, no lock) while a foreign edge is recorded and evaluated.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `CLI.md` (`dep`, new `project` command),
  `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md` and `README.md` document cross-repo dependencies,
  the discovery rule, the fail-safe `unresolved` behaviour and the clone
  remediation; `wl dep --help` states that foreign ids are supported.
- **AC7 — Full suite green.** The ContextHub suite passes via the test skill
  with no duplicate collection and no cache-key collision, including the new
  cross-repo test module.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/dep.ts` — accept and validate foreign endpoints, JSON fields
- `src/commands/project.ts` — **new**: `wl project list|add` (discovery +
  clone remediation)
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase`/`normalizeCliId` and any new resolver hook
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `isGenuineWorklogStore` (reused) + projects-root resolution
- `src/config.ts` — `projectsRoot` and prefix→path mapping
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` — `isDependencyActive` /
  `getActiveDependencyBlockers` foreign-target resolution and fail-safe
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` — `buildEdgeCache` (foreign items
  cannot be in the local edge cache; the resolver must not assume they are)
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — blocked-candidate filtering
  and blocker surfacing for foreign blockers
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — dependency check reporting unresolved foreign edges
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts`, `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — isolation guards
  (expected unchanged; regression-pinned)
- `tests/cross-repo-dependencies.test.ts` — **new** primary test module
- `tests/database-dependencies-comments-extraction.test.ts`,
  `tests/doctor-dependency-check.test.ts` — regression
- `CLI.md`, `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md`, `README.md` — documentation

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: scanning cost / surprise I/O.** Mitigation: one readdir of the
  projects root plus two `existsSync` probes per candidate, memoised per process;
  a missing/unreadable projects root is a warning, never an error.
- **Risk: ambiguity.** Two projects claiming the same prefix cannot be resolved
  safely → report, do not guess (probe-by-lookup, as the TUI resolver does, is
  acceptable only when it disambiguates a single owner).
- **Risk: semantic change for existing consumers.** Today the *framework* treats
  cross-prefix edges as coordination notes and never blocks on them. If the
  resolver starts returning `unresolved`-blocked for such edges, a consumer that
  previously ignored them could stall. Mitigation: fail-safe is `blocked` only
  when a real foreign store is discovered; an undiscoverable prefix stays a
  non-blocking coordination note until `wl project add` resolves it — state this
  explicitly in the JSON (`foreign_dependency: "resolved" | "unresolved" |
  "unavailable"`).
- **Assumption (documented, producer confirmable):** projects are siblings under
  a common projects root (today `/home/rgardler/projects/<project>`), each with
  its own `.worklog/` and a distinct `prefix` in `config.yaml`.
- **Assumption:** `git clone` uses the operator's existing git credentials; the
  tool never prompts for credentials.
- **Risk: TUI/skills duplication drift.** Mitigation: D6 names the follow-ups;
  this item does not edit the TUI or the skills.

## Out of scope

- Making the SorraAgents implement skill gate on cross-repo edges (separate
  framework item; recorded in Related work).
- Cross-*machine* / remote-store dependencies (only local sibling clones).
- Auto-cloning without a producer-supplied URL.
- Merging or syncing foreign stores, or exposing their items in this project's
  list/search surfaces (only dependency resolution reads them).

## Related work

- **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** (llm) — the consumer item that needs a *resolvable*
  cross-repo edge to its upstream SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB; it is parked awaiting
  that upstream fix and this capability.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** (SorraAgents) — the "cross-project edges are
  coordination notes, never blocking" assumption this work supersedes.
- **WL-0MVGB23MM004X501** — TUI footer prefix→sibling resolution (the first
  in-tree copy of the scan).
- **WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST** — cross-project sync guard (the isolation contract D5
  must keep).
- **WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF** — shared `wl next`/`wl worklist` browse feed (the
  single selection path that AC3 must extend, not fork).
## Plan (plan_complete, 2026-10-31)

### Feature breakdown — tracer-bullet vertical slices, test-first

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Cross-repo fixture harness and discovery spec (WL-0MVWEEK24000S3TW) | task | — | AC1 |
| F2 | Discovery module and `wl project list` (WL-0MVWEELAW005SDLU) | feature | F1 | AC1, D1, D6 |
| F3 | Foreign dependency edge and isolation spec (WL-0MVWEEMP2002N37W) | task | F2 | AC2, AC5 |
| F4 | Foreign dependency edge CRUD (WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC) | feature | F3 | AC2, D2 |
| F5 | Foreign blocker gating and fail-safe spec (WL-0MVWEEP4U003FR91) | task | F4 | AC3 |
| F6 | Resolve foreign blockers in gating paths (WL-0MVWEEQ8K0013DOY) | feature | F5 | AC3, D3 |
| F7 | Project add remediation and clone spec (WL-0MVWEER72000TT6G) | task | F6 | AC4 |
| F8 | Implement `wl project add` and remediation (WL-0MVWEES9J0035SG6) | feature | F7 | AC4, D4 |
| F9 | Cross-repo dependency documentation (WL-0MVWEETA9006LFED) | docs | F8 | AC6 |
| F10 | Sync isolation and full-suite verification (WL-0MVWEEU5Z004E4K1) | task | F9 | AC5, AC7 |

Each child is a vertical slice through code, tests, docs and observability
(JSON fields, `wl doctor` findings, debug logging). Test/verification children
(F1, F3, F5, F7, F10) are ordered **before** the implementation child that turns
them green, per the test-first rule.

### Phasing (between-phase guidance)

- **Phase 1 — discovery (F1→F2).** After F2 lands, re-read F3/F4 descriptions:
  the discovery API shape (`discoverProjects`) is now concrete, so F3's fixture
  usage and F4's resolver signature should be checked against it before starting.
- **Phase 2 — foreign edges (F3→F4).** After F4, re-read F5/F6: the
  `foreign_dependency` tri-state is now implemented, so F5's gating assertions
  must match the emitted field names exactly.
- **Phase 3 — gating (F5→F6).** After F6, re-read F7/F8: the `unknown_project`
  payload is shared between `dep` and `next`, so F7 must assert the same shape
  F6 emits for `unresolved`.
- **Phase 4 — remediation (F7→F8).** After F8, F9 documents only behaviour that
  is now test-covered; F10 then verifies isolation and the full suite.

### Sequencing note

The chain is declared strictly linear (F1→F2→…→F10) for a single implementer.
F7's only technical prerequisite is F2 (discovery), and F9's are F6+F8; the
extra edges are deliberate serialisation, not hard dependencies.

### Deliberately deferred (out of scope, per this item)

Per **D6** and "Out of scope", the two existing prefix→sibling scan copies are
**not** converted here and no follow-up items are created yet (this item's own
wording: "create as `discovered-from` once this lands"):

- TUI title resolver — `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/work-item-title.ts`
  (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501).
- Skills layer — `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`).
- SorraAgents implement-skill gating on resolvable cross-repo edges
  (SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T) — separate framework item.

### Reused existing implementations (no new duplication)

- `isGenuineWorklogStore()` — `src/worklog-paths.ts` (worktree-stub discriminator, D1).
- `isDependencyActive()` — `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`
  (terminal semantics reused, never forked, D3).
- `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` (`src/sync/repo-context.ts`) and
  `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` (`src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`) — isolation guards
  kept and regression-pinned (D5).
- `tests/test-utils.ts` temp-dir helpers; `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` CLI harness.
- Lazy command registry pattern — `src/command-registry.ts` (for `wl project`).

### Documented assumptions (producer confirmable)

1. **Projects are siblings under a common root** (today `/home/rgardler/projects/<project>`),
   each with its own `.worklog/` and a distinct `prefix`. Default `projectsRoot`
   is the parent directory of the current checkout's git root.
2. **Config storage for the mapping**: `projectsRoot` plus a `projects:` map
   (`<PREFIX>: { path, gitUrl }`) live in `.worklog/config.yaml`, matching the
   item's "records the mapping in the project config". No new config file.
3. **Git credentials** come from the operator's existing git configuration; the
   tool never prompts for credentials (item's stated assumption).
4. **`--interactive` is opt-in only**; every default path is non-interactive so
   agents (which cannot answer prompts) never hang.
5. **Unknown-prefix compatibility**: an undiscoverable prefix stays a
   non-blocking `foreign_dependency: "unavailable"` coordination note, so
   existing consumers that ignored cross-prefix edges do not stall (item risk
   mitigation, made explicit in the JSON).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking questions were needed: the item already carried a full design
(D1–D6), seven acceptance criteria and a predicted key-file list, so the
planning decisions below were resolvable from the item and the codebase. Each is
recorded as a **decision with evidence** rather than an invented answer.

- **Q (self-answered): Is the autoplan pre-check's `skip` decision authoritative?**
  Answer (plan agent): No. `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` returned
  `Extra Small` / `Low`, but the effort-and-risk run recorded O=M=P=0.00h, risk
  0/25 and `assumptions: ["Auto-generated by autoplan decision"]` with no WBS —

# Recurrence: `packages/shared` wiped from the main checkout (2026-10-31) — wl broken machine-wide

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Status source:** AH-0MVVNKP1B00701HR

## Problem statement

For the second time in five days (previous: 2026-10-26, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG),
a concurrent, worktree-scoped agent run deleted every tracked file under
`packages/shared/` from the main ContextHub checkout, plus the gitignored
`packages/shared/dist/` build output. Because `wl` resolves
`@worklog/shared/worklog-paths` from that build output, **every `wl`
invocation on the machine failed for ~35 minutes** until an AI_Hell session
repaired it, blocking every agent in ContextHub, AI_Hell and
any other project using the shared `wl` CLI. The 2026-10-26 hardening (the
finish main-checkout guard + `guarded_run_all`, shipped in v1.0.24) did **not**
prevent this event, so the guard's coverage must be re-examined rather than
re-applied.

## Users

- **All agents on the host** (ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, …) — `wl` is the
  single source of truth for work tracking; a broken `wl` fails closed for
  every agent machine-wide.
  - *User story:* "As an agent finishing a work item, I want the main checkout
    protected from foreign deletions, so that my `wl` commands never die with
    'the shared workspace build output is missing'."
- **The developer/operator (producer)** — must be able to recover in one step
  and to trust `finish`'s guard report.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, I want a one-command recovery and a loud,
    named cause, so a wipe never costs 35 minutes of machine-wide downtime."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Forensic determination recorded.** A written timeline and actor
  determination for the 2026-10-31 wipe live in this item's description:
  who/what deleted `packages/shared`, with evidence. Where the actor cannot be
  proven after the fact, the item records what was ruled out and names the
  residual hypothesis (precedent: WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG AC1).
- **AC2 — ContextHub-side integrity check.** A check that runs independently of
  `implement.py finish` (e.g. `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` or a new
  `scripts/check-main-checkout.sh`) detects tracked-file deletions in the main
  checkout and fails loudly, naming every deleted path and the concurrent
  actor evidence — so deletions are reported even when the overlapping finish
  run aborts at the test gate (the 2026-10-31 run's `verifies: []` gap).
  Covered by a regression test.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic fires on this exact state.** `wl`'s missing-shared-dist
  diagnostic is confirmed (test) to fire when tracked sources *and* `dist/`
  are gone, and its remediation text covers both `git restore`/`git checkout`
  for deleted tracked files and `npm run build:shared` for the gitignored
  output.
- **AC4 — One-step recovery.** A runbook exists in `docs/dev/` restoring
  `packages/shared` from git + `npm run build:shared`, **and** a
  `scripts/repair-shared-package.sh` (producer decision: Option B) performs
  the restore in one command — deleted tracked files from HEAD, then `dist/`
  rebuild — with a smoke test.
- **AC5 — Validation.** Regression tests cover AC2–AC4 (AC1 is a written
  forensic record, validated by review rather than by a test); all related
  documentation (this item's runbook, `docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md`,
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, code comments) is updated to reflect the
  changes; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> **Moved to SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM (producer decision, Option C):** the
> `implement.py` finish-guard hardening (failure-path verification +
> cross-checkout attribution) ships in the SorraAgents repo under that item.
> This item tracks the ContextHub-side deliverables (AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5) and
> cross-references it; the SorraAgents item cross-references this one.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundaries.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` lives in
  the SorraAgents repo (`~/projects/SorraAgents`). The producer authorises the
  guard changes there under **SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM** (linked work item); this
  item makes no agent-infrastructure edits.
- **No weakening of existing guards.** The 2026-10-26 main-checkout guard
  (fail-loud on deletions, `own_churn` allow-list, single-owner finish lock)
  and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` invariants must stay intact.
- **Non-destructive recovery.** Restoring from git must never stash, reset or
  discard content; deletions are recoverable because every path exists in
  `HEAD`.
- **`wl` is single source of truth.** Detection/reporting must use `wl`
  comments and the work-item audit trail so the report survives the status
  reset on abort.

## Existing state

- **Shipped hardening (v1.0.24, 2026-10-26):** finish main-checkout guard
  (snapshot at start; verify at pre-push and pre-worktree-removal; deletions
  never allow-listed; loud abort naming paths + actor evidence;
  WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q), single-owner finish lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84),
  `guarded_run_all`, and the `wl` missing-shared-dist preflight diagnostic
  (`src/cli.ts`, tests/cli/missing-shared-dist.test.ts,
  docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md).
- **What still failed on 2026-10-31:**
  - The finish run that overlapped the wipe
    (`.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log`, WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6) shows
    `main_checkout_guard` with `snapshot_at` 14:43:06, `baseline_paths: 2`,
    **`verifies: []`** — it aborted at the test gate (test run 1/3 failed at
    14:58) before any verify point, so the guard never evaluated the 37
    deletions and reported nothing.
  - **New timing correlation:** the gate's test slot was acquired at
    ~14:52:56 (queued_at 1793457862.761 + wait 513.812s) and the full-scope
    suite started ≈14:53 — the exact minute of the `packages/shared/` mtime.
    The full-scope gate suite (in the worktree, driven by the would-be-commit
    index) is the strongest remaining suspect window; a separate
    finish-run *postbuild* also runs `scripts/install-herdr.sh` → `npm ci`
    against the main checkout (the WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT defect class), though
    that only destroys the workspace *link*, not tracked sources.
  - The AI_Hell finish guard reported `own_churn` paths belonging to **other
    work items** (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, five `src/powerups/*`,
    `src/vfx/droneFeel.docs.test.ts`) while its own main checkout stayed clean
    — attribution/resolution can pull paths from outside the repo being
    finished; the guard's write-surface audit is tracked under
    SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM.
- **Distinguishing this wipe:** tracked sources *and* `dist/` were removed
  (37 `D` entries + missing build output) — a whole-directory removal, not the
  `rimraf dist`-only hypothesis from 2026-10-26.

## Desired change

1. Report main-checkout deletions independently of a finish run that may abort
   at the gate (AC2, this item) — the finish-side failure-path verification
   itself is SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM.
2. Extend the `wl` diagnostic to the tracked-sources-gone state (AC3).
3. Provide one-step recovery: runbook + `repair-shared-package.sh` (AC4).
4. Record the definitive timeline/actor determination (AC1).

## Plan (implementation sequence)

Test-first: each step lands its regression test together with the code it
covers. No new children — the item is a single Small (~11h expected) slice.

1. **AC1 — Forensics (documentation only).** Assemble the timeline from
   `.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log` (guard record, `verifies: []`), the test
   slot timing (acquired ~14:52:56, full-scope suite start ≈14:53), the
   `packages/shared/` mtime, the concurrent finish-run logs and `git reflog`;
   record the timeline, the ruled-out hypotheses and the residual hypothesis in
   this item's description. Evidence lives in `wl`, not in a repo file.
2. **AC2 — Independent integrity check.** New `scripts/check-main-checkout.sh`:
   git-level check at the main checkout root (`git status --porcelain
   --untracked-files=no`, `D` entries = deletions), fail non-zero naming every
   deleted path plus concurrent-actor evidence, and report through
   `wl comment add` so the report survives an aborted finish run. Regression
   test `tests/scripts/check-main-checkout.test.ts` on a scratch git repo:
   clean passes, one deletion fails naming the path, concurrent-churn scenario.
3. **AC3 — Diagnostic covers the tracked-sources-gone state.** Planning found
   the gap: `expectedSharedDistArtifactPath()` discovers the repo root through
   `packages/shared/package.json`, so when the tracked sources *and* `dist/` are
   gone it returns `null` and `sharedDistPreflight()` stays silent (fail-open) —
   exactly the 2026-10-31 state. Fix root discovery so it does not depend on
   `packages/shared/package.json` surviving, and extend
   `missingSharedDistDiagnostic()` remediation text to cover both
   `git restore`/`git checkout --` for deleted tracked files and
   `npm run build:shared` for the gitignored output. Extend
   `tests/cli/missing-shared-dist.test.ts` with the both-gone fixture.
4. **AC4 — One-step recovery.** `scripts/repair-shared-package.sh`: restore
   deleted tracked files from `HEAD` (`git checkout -- packages/shared`, never
   stash/reset), then `npm run build:shared`; idempotent, non-destructive,
   non-zero exit with a named cause on failure. Runbook in
   `docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md` (recovery section) plus a pointer
   from `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`. Smoke test
   `tests/scripts/repair-shared-package.test.ts` on a scratch clone: delete a
   tracked file + `dist/`, run the script, assert both are restored.
5. **AC5 — Docs + full suite.** Update `src/cli.ts` comments, the diagnostic
   doc and the worktree-isolation doc; run the full suite via the test skill.

**Scope note (AC2 path):** no `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` exists in this repo
(the reference in `AGENTS.md` is stale), so AC2's example resolves to the new
`scripts/check-main-checkout.sh`.

**Reuse check:** `sharedDistPreflight()` / `missingSharedDistDiagnostic()` and
`tests/cli/missing-shared-dist.test.ts` are extended rather than duplicated; no
existing main-checkout integrity script exists to reuse.

## Key Files

- `src/cli.ts` + `tests/cli/missing-shared-dist.test.ts` — `wl` preflight
  diagnostic (AC3).
- `scripts/check-main-checkout.sh` (new) +
  `tests/scripts/check-main-checkout.test.ts` — ContextHub-side integrity check
  (AC2).
- `docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` —
  docs to update.
- `packages/shared/package.json`, `packages/shared/src/**`, `package.json`
  (`build:shared`, `@worklog/shared: file:./packages/shared`).
- `.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log` — the 2026-10-31 finish log (evidence).
- `scripts/repair-shared-package.sh` (new) +
  `tests/scripts/repair-shared-package.test.ts` (smoke test, AC4).

## Related work

- **SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM** — *Finish main-checkout guard: failure-path
  verification + cross-checkout attribution* (SorraAgents, open) — owns the
  `implement.py` guard ACs (was this item's AC2/AC3); cross-referenced.
- **WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG** — predecessor: *Implement.py finish wiped
  packages/shared from main checkout* (2026-10-26), completed/shipped v1.0.24;
  source of AC1's ruling-out precedent and the guard's design.
- **WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q** — *Finish aborts loudly on foreign main-checkout
  deletions* (completed) — the existing fail-loud deletion guard.
- **WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84** — *Single-owner lock for the main checkout during
  finish* (completed) — per-repo lock; does not cover cross-repo concurrency.
- **WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT** — *herdr postbuild npm ci in a worktree build wipes
  the @worklog/shared workspace link* (open, plan_complete) — different defect
  (link only, npm-ci-driven); partial overlap on the wl-broken symptom.
- **WL-0MVPE2DXB00978T5** — *wl diagnostic when the shared build output is
  missing* (completed) — AC3's existing diagnostic.
- **WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET** — *implement.py finish can fast-forward the main
  checkout's dev mid-test-run, producing phantom test failures* (open) —
  concurrency during the gate.
- **AH-0MVVNKP1B00701HR** — the AI_Hell session that discovered and repaired
  the wipe (in_review).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (forensics vs prevention).** Actor determination (AC1) is
  after-the-fact and the evidence is partially destroyed; chasing a provable
  actor could consume the whole item. Mitigation: AC1 is bounded by the
  ruling-out bar (below); prevention (AC2 + SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM), diagnostic
  (AC3) and recovery (AC4) carry the value. Linked opportunities are recorded
  as work items, not folded into this one.
- **Guard false positives.** Tightening detection (AC2, and the SA item's
  guard changes) risks aborting legitimate agent activity on benign concurrent
  churn (the SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG defect class). Mitigation: keep the
  `own_churn`/expected-dirty allow-lists, treat deletions as never
  allow-listed, and cover both clean and foreign-churn scenarios with
  regression tests.
- **Cross-repo concurrency is out of the finish lock's scope.** The per-repo
  finish lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) does not serialise two checkouts' worth of
  runs; AC2's independent check and the SA item's read-only/attribution audit
  are the mitigations — serialisation across repos is a linked opportunity,
  not in scope.

## Assumptions

- **Ruling-out bar for AC1 (precedent-based):** like WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG AC1,
  conclusive actor proof is only required where the evidence permits;
  otherwise the item records the ruled-out hypotheses and the residual
  hypothesis. The 14:53 gate-start correlation is the primary residual lead;
  `npm ci`/install-herdr postbuild (link wipe) is a ruled-out mechanism for
  *tracked-source* deletion unless new evidence appears.
- Detection must be reported through `wl` comments (survives abort) and the
  runbook/script recovery must be non-destructive.
- Producer decisions applied 2026-10-31: **Q1 → Option C** (guard change ships
  in SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM; this item keeps ContextHub-side deliverables) and
  **Q2 → Option B** (AC4 includes the automated `repair-shared-package.sh`
  script with a smoke test). Evidence: interactive producer reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84** – Single-owner lock for the main checkout during finish (completed)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 53z, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+168 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-31T22:22Z (plan skill, Map): effort/risk pre-check returned
  effort=Small, risk=Low → no decomposition; ran the six automated review
  stages on the existing content. Changes made: (a) AC5 reworded so test
  coverage is claimed for AC2–AC4 only (a forensic narrative cannot be
  regression-tested); (b) `## Plan (implementation sequence)` block added,

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **Where should the guard change ship (AC2/AC3)?**
  - Asked: 2026-10-31 (intake handoff); options A (cross-repo change from

  - **Answer (producer): "2. B"** — Option B: docs runbook **and** the

    interactive producer reply (2026-10-31).

    caused by manual multi-step recovery (copy from a worktree, then rebuild);
    `docs/dev/wl-shared-dist-diagnostic.md` covers the dist-missing case only,
    not deleted tracked sources.
- Duplicate-work check: searched `packages/shared wiped`, `shared workspace
  build output`, `implement finish guard`. No fully-overlapping completed item:
  the predecessor WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG is completed but provably did not

## AC1 — Forensic record: 2026-10-31 timeline and actor determination

Written timeline and actor determination for the 2026-10-31 wipe, per AC1.
Evidence sources: `.worklog/logs/finish-child4d.log` (the overlapping finish
run for WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6), the gate test-slot timing, `packages/shared`
file mtimes and `git reflog`. The evidence is partially destroyed (the repair
restored files from git, rewriting mtimes), so the ruling-out bar follows the
WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG precedent: conclusive proof only where the evidence
permits; otherwise the residual hypothesis below.

### Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-31)

| Time | Event | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 14:43:06 | Finish gate starts for WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6: `main_checkout_guard` snapshot taken in `finish-child4d.log` — `baseline_paths: 2` (the two staged regression tests), `own_churn: []`, **`verifies: []`** | `finish-child4d.log` guard JSON |
| 14:43–14:44 | Build OK: `npm run build` succeeded in the finish worktree; postbuild `install-herdr.sh` ran `npm ci` against the main checkout's `packages/herdr` | `finish-child4d.log` build stdout |
| ≈14:52:56 | Gate test slot acquired (`queued_at=1793457862.761` + `wait_seconds=513.812`) | `finish-child4d.log` run_tests notice |
| ≈14:53 | Full-scope gate suite (v1.0.24) started in the finish worktree — the minute the `packages/shared` mtime marked the wipe | slot timing + mtime correlation |
| 14:58 | Test run 1/3 FAILED (`test_failure`); 104× `wl create failed: node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:275` across init/sync/stats/plugin suites — `@worklog/shared` resolution was already broken: the main checkout's `packages/shared` (sources + `dist/`) was gone | `finish-child4d.log` failures array |
| 14:58 | Run aborted at the gate — **no guard verify point was reached**, so `verifies: []` and nothing reported the 37 deletions. This reporting gap is what AC2 closes | `finish-child4d.log` report |
| 15:01 | AI_Hell session (AH-0MVVNKP1B00701HR) repaired `packages/shared` (restore + rebuild) | `packages/shared/package.json` mtime 15:01:31 (restore-time write) |

### Ruled out

- **`npm ci` / `install-herdr.sh` postbuild** — ran at ≈14:44 against the main
  checkout's `packages/herdr`; that defect class only destroys the workspace
  *link* (`node_modules/@worklog/shared`), never tracked sources
  (WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT). Its stdout shows successful link operations and no
  source deletion; and it ran ~9 minutes before the wipe minute, not at it.
- **The overlapping finish run itself writing outside its worktree** — its
  staged changes were the two regression test files; a guard verify point
  would have caught foreign deletions had one been reached. Nothing in the
  log indicates worktree-escape writes.
- **A `wl`-internal operation** — `wl` never mutates `packages/shared`
  sources.

### Residual hypothesis (actor unproven)

A **concurrent, worktree-scoped agent run other than the finish run**
deleted the whole `packages/shared` directory (tracked sources *and*
gitignored `dist/` — a whole-directory removal, unlike the 2026-10-26
rimraf-dist-only shape). Timing places the wipe at ≈14:53 — the exact minute
the full-scope gate suite started — and the `wl create failed` resolution
errors at 14:58 prove the state existed mid-gate. That gate window is the
**primary residual lead**; however, no mechanism by which the worktree's gate
suite deletes the main checkout's `packages/shared` has been established (the
worktree's `node_modules` is symlinked to the main checkout's — building in a
worktree does not clean the main checkout's workspace directory, and the
WL-0MVWJ4IKT005SAHT fix made `npm ci` refuse to run from worktrees). The
actor is therefore recorded as **unproven**; the mechanism class (foreign
worktree-scoped run) is shared with the 2026-10-26 incident. Prevention of
the *reporting* gap ships here (AC2 `scripts/check-main-checkout.sh` —
independent of a finish run that may abort at the gate) and in
SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM (failure-path verification + cross-checkout attribution);
one-step recovery ships as AC4 `scripts/repair-shared-package.sh`.

# CLI git test fixtures inherit GIT_INDEX_FILE, breaking implement.py finish gate attribution

## Problem statement

Several CLI test fixtures build a "real git" environment by spreading `process.env`, so they inherit any repository-override variable the caller exported — notably `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, which `implement.py finish` sets to a temporary index (`implement-gate-*.index`) while it validates the would-be-commit tree. Fixture `git add`/`git commit` then stage into the gate's index, so the gate correctly refuses the run as unattributable ("gate evidence invalid: the temporary index changed while the suite ran") and the fixture itself fails with `invalid object … for '.worklog/config.yaml'` / `Error building trees`.

## Users

- **Implementing agents** (primary). User story: *As an agent running `implement.py finish`, I want the gate verdict to describe my change, so that a green tree is not blocked by an unrelated fixture leaking into the gate's index.*
- **Developers running the full suite** with a repository-override variable exported (e.g. from a git hook) — user story: *As a developer, I want `npm test` to behave identically whether or not `GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_DIR` is set in my shell.*
- **Release/audit pipeline** — the finish gate is the pre-commit evidence source; an unattributable verdict stalls the `dev` push gate.

## Existing state (verified in this checkout, 2026-11-01)

- **A suite-wide guard already landed**: `tests/setup-tests.ts` deletes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` and the `GIT_CONFIG*` family once, before any test file runs (WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61, commit `d5241210`). This covers the *suite-level* leak but not fixtures handed a non-hermetic env by a test, nor a future re-introduction of the spread.
- **One fixture-level implementation exists but is local**: `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` defines its own hermetic env helper and a "leaked `GIT_INDEX_FILE`" regression test (same item, `WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61`). It is not shared, and ~12 other fixtures still spread `process.env`.
- **Still non-hermetic** (`realGitEnv()` = `{ ...process.env, PATH: realGitPath() }`): `tests/cli/sync-delta-pull.test.ts`, `sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`, `sync-delta-fallback.test.ts`, `sync-phase-timings.test.ts`, `sync-claim-revert.test.ts`, `sync-audit-newest-wins.test.ts`, `sync-delta-push.test.ts`, `sync-integration-convergence.test.ts`, `sync-delta-delete.test.ts`, `doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts`. Also inline `{ ...process.env, PATH: realGitPath() }`: `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-cache-invalidation.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` (line ~130).
- **Canonical Python precedent**: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::fixture_git_env()` scrubs repository overrides and then pops `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, with a docstring explaining exactly this gate interaction. The TS helper should mirror it (the Python file is a reference, not a change target).
- **Workaround used while discovering this** (WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82): `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND='env -u GIT_INDEX_FILE npm --silent test -- tests'` — still runs the full suite at the gate while shielding non-hermetic fixtures.

## Desired change

Introduce one shared TypeScript fixture helper that mirrors `fixture_git_env()`, route every fixture git invocation through it, add a regression test that proves an inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE` cannot be mutated, and confirm the finish gate reports an unchanged index on a tree that touches an affected fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A shared `fixtureGitEnv(base?)` helper exists in `tests/cli/git-helpers.ts` that (a) returns a copy of the given/base environment, (b) removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` and `GIT_CONFIG`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`/`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, and (c) lets an explicitly supplied value win (so tests that deliberately target an index/`GIT_DIR` still work). It mirrors `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::fixture_git_env()`.
- [ ] Every fixture that spawns `git` with a spread of `process.env` uses that helper — no remaining `realGitEnv()`/inline `{ ...process.env, PATH: realGitPath() }` handed to a git invocation. Asserted by a test (grep-style scan of `tests/`) so the property cannot silently regress.
- [ ] A regression test proves a fixture-driven `git add` + `git commit` leaves an inherited `GIT_INDEX_FILE` byte-identical (and commits into its own repository), i.e. the leak the gate reported is impossible.
- [ ] `implement.py finish` on a tree touching `tests/cli/sync-delta-pull.test.ts` reports `index_unchanged: true` in the gate summary with no "gate evidence invalid" notice, without the `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND` workaround.
- [ ] Behaviour is unchanged when no override variable is exported (fixtures still use the real git binary, still honour `PATH` with `tests/cli/mock-bin` removed).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Test-only change: no product (`src/`) behaviour change; no changes under `skill/` or `.pi/`.
- Must not weaken tests that deliberately exercise a leaked override — `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (`GIT_DIR` leak defence), `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` (leaked-index regression) — explicit values must win over the scrub.
- Must keep the `PATH` behaviour of `realGitEnv()`/`realGitPath()` (mock-bin removed) so fixtures still reach the real git binary.
- Do not rely solely on `tests/setup-tests.ts` ordering; the fixture-level guard must hold even if a test sets an override after setup has run.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption**: the suite-wide `setup-tests.ts` scrub stays; this work is defence-in-depth plus an enforceable invariant (AC2), not a replacement.
- **Risk (over-scrubbing hides real bugs)**: scrubbing in fixtures could mask a genuine product-side repository-override leak. *Mitigation*: product-side sanitisation (`src/sync/git-exec.ts`) keeps its own tests, and explicit-value-wins keeps the deliberate-leak tests meaningful.
- **Risk (scope creep)**: "make every test spawn hermetic" (HOME, `GIT_CONFIG`, locale, TZ) is much larger than this item. *Mitigation*: limit scope to git repository-override variables; record anything else as a separate linked item rather than widening this one.
- **Risk (gate verification is environment-dependent)**: AC4 needs a real `implement.py finish` run; if the gate cannot be exercised in-session, record the observed gate summary JSON as evidence and note the residual gap.
- **Risk (duplicate work)**: an older open item (`WL-0MVVKS02A004EVMJ`) tracked the same defect; it has been closed as a duplicate and its content absorbed here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/cli/git-helpers.ts` — Add `fixtureGitEnv()` (mirroring `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::fixture_git_env()`), alongside the existing `initRepo`/`initBareRepo`.
- `tests/cli/sync-delta-pull.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-delta-fallback.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-phase-timings.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-audit-newest-wins.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-delta-push.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-integration-convergence.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-delta-delete.test.ts`, `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` — Replace local `realGitEnv()` with the shared helper.
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-cache-invalidation.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` — Use the shared helper (drop the duplicated local hermetic helper/inline spread).
- `tests/cli/fixture-git-env.test.ts` (new) — Regression test for the inherited-`GIT_INDEX_FILE` case + the no-non-hermetic-fixtures invariant scan.
- `tests/setup-tests.ts` — Reference only (existing suite-wide scrub); comment cross-link to the new helper.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Reference implementation (`fixture_git_env()`); no change.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — Document the fixture-env invariant next to the existing `GIT_INDEX_FILE` gate notes.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVVKS02A004EVMJ` — *Harden finish-gate full-suite runs against non-hermetic git fixtures (GIT_INDEX_FILE)* — closed as a **duplicate** of this item; its scope (~20 affected fixtures, the `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND` workaround, the `fixture_git_env()` precedent) is absorbed here.
- `WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61` (completed) — *sync-concurrent test fixture leaks GIT_INDEX_FILE into its fixture repos* — landed the `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts` local hermetic helper, its leaked-index regression test, and the suite-wide scrub in `tests/setup-tests.ts` (commit `d5241210`). This item generalises that fix.
- `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` (completed) — discovery source; its children `WL-0MVTVYXZD002NDMP` and `WL-0MVTVZHFU000PRT6` hit the "gate evidence invalid" failure at `finish`.
- `WL-0MS99Y6R40028Q9G` (completed) — `wl sync` in a worktree commits the whole tree as deleted — the `GIT_DIR` leak-defence precedent in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `src/sync/git-exec.ts`.
- SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 / SA-0MVQHVGFR006W8LG — the finish-gate temporary-index design that makes the leak fatal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (problem, observed gate output, workaround, affected fixtures, four testable ACs) was sufficient to draft a brief, and the remaining unknowns were resolved by repository inspection rather than by asking the operator.

- **Q (self-answered by repo inspection)**: "Is the fixture leak already fixed by the suite-wide scrub in `tests/setup-tests.ts`?" — Answer: partially. The scrub landed via `WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61` (commit `d5241210`) and removes the variables once before the suite runs; fixtures that spread `process.env` at call time are still non-hermetic on their own, and `sync-concurrent.test.ts` is the only fixture with a local guard. Evidence: `tests/setup-tests.ts:42-68`, `tests/cli/sync-concurrent.test.ts:43-64`.
- **Q (self-answered)**: "Duplicate work?" — Duplicate check performed (`wl search` on `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `fixture git env`, `gate evidence invalid`, `realGitEnv`). `WL-0MVVKS02A004EVMJ` (open, medium chore) covered the same root cause with a near-identical AC set; consolidated here (closed as duplicate, content absorbed) so the work is not dispatched twice. `WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61` (completed) is a partial predecessor covering one fixture plus the suite-wide scrub.
- **Q (self-answered)**: "How many fixtures are affected?" — 10 files define `realGitEnv()` spreading `process.env`, and 3 more inline the same spread for git calls (13 total). Evidence: `rg -n "function realGitEnv" tests/`, `rg -n "realGitPath" tests/`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking)**: whether the `fixtureGitEnv()` helper should also scrub `GIT_CONFIG*` or leave config handling to callers — resolved as "scrub, matching `setup-tests.ts`", revisitable during implementation if a fixture needs ambient config.

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVVKS02A004EVMJ** – Harden finish-gate full-suite runs against non-hermetic git fixtures (GIT_INDEX_FILE) (completed)
- **WL-0MVVWRPRO006IQ61** – sync-concurrent test fixture leaks GIT_INDEX_FILE into its fixture repos (completed)

# F0 — Machine-budget test harness and two-instance isolation fixture

Parent: WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB (Host-wide concurrency budget for implement and audit dispatches)

## Goal

As a future maintainer, I need one reusable harness that models two herdr
instances sharing a single machine coordination dir, so every host-budget test
asserts the same machine-scoped semantics instead of hand-rolling temp dirs,
fake instance ids and fake pane lists per test file.

## Scope

Test-support only — **no production behaviour changes** in this item. This is
the test/verification slice that lands before the ledger implementation
(test-first ordering).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A shared fixture module exports: `withMachineDir(fn)` (isolated temp dir +
   guaranteed cleanup), `makeInstance(id)` (fake instance record),
   `makeLivePaneList(panes)` and a raw ledger writer/seeder used to set up
   pre-existing entries without going through the production API.
2. The fixture pins the coordination dir via `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` (or an
   injected dir path) so no test can touch the real `~/.herdr/downtime`.
3. A self-test proves isolation: two fake instances over one temp dir observe
   each other's writes; a second `withMachineDir` call resolves to a distinct
   dir; cleanup leaves no residue in the temp root.
4. The fixture header comment names the `slot-budget-machine.test.ts`
   precedent (WL-0MTII48OV008P2QU) and documents the fake-pane-list contract.
5. `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass (the harness is green
   on its own, so it never lands as a red test-only commit).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.test.ts` (new)
- reference: `packages/herdr/src/slot-budget-machine.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extract the temp-dir + instance-id + cleanup helpers used by
   `slot-budget-machine.test.ts` into a fixture module.
2. Model the live pane list as a plain `Array<{ paneId: string; title: string }>`
   so tests drive liveness without herdr or `/proc`.
3. Add a raw JSON writer for the ledger file so tests can seed stale,
   corrupt and override entries directly.
4. Self-test the harness (isolation + cleanup) — pass/fail on its own.

## Dependencies

None.

# CORRECTION (2026-11-01 19:45) — this is a kernel panic after all

**The earlier classification in this description ("hardware/firmware freeze, not a kernel panic") was
wrong and is superseded by this section.** It is retained below for the audit trail, but do not act on
it without reading this.

## What overturned it

The operator deliberately triggered a SysRq crash (`echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger`, which performs a
NULL-pointer panic) at 2026-11-01 19:38:58. Result:

- The caps-lock LED blinked **consistently at ~1 blink per 0.5 s** — the same signature the operator
  reports for the unexplained crashes. That is the **Linux kernel panic LED blink**, not an EC fault
  code. Linux does blink keyboard LEDs from the panic loop.
- The machine **rebooted by itself** (next boot 19:40:42, ~104 s later).
- **No vmcore was produced, and pstore stayed empty** — exactly as with every "mysterious" crash.

So the earlier "no panic was recorded, therefore it was not a panic" inference was invalid: the absence
of evidence was never evidence of absence. It was four independent capture failures:

| Why nothing was captured | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **crashkernel reservation is too small** | `kdump-config show` reports `crashkernel suggested size: 1103M`; the reservation is **512M** (`crashkernel=…,4G-32G:512M,…`, MemTotal 30.3 GiB). `crashkernel addr: 0x` is empty. The crash kernel cannot boot, so the dump fails and the machine reboots empty. |
| **pstore cannot work on this firmware** | `efi_pstore` is loaded but `/sys/firmware/efi/efivars` contains **no dump/OOPS variable store**, so the backend has nothing to write to. Confirmed dead end; kdump is the only viable path. |
| **journald cannot flush at panic** | Journal always stops mid-sentence; the panic text goes to the console only. |
| **`quiet splash` hides the console** | Even the panic banner and stack were never visible on screen. |

## Revised understanding

The unexplained crashes **do reach `panic()`** — they are kernel oops/BUG/panic events in a driver or
subsystem, not power loss and not a thermal cut-out. Supporting timing evidence: `kernel.panic=5` was
introduced on 2026-10-18 (`/etc/sysctl.d/99-panic-autoreboot.conf`), and the boot -4 → -3 gap on
2026-10-30 was only **18 s** (21:34:28 → 21:34:46), the signature of a panic auto-reboot. Crashes that
sat "dead" until a manual power-cycle are explained by `crash_kexec()` being invoked into the undersized
crash region and hanging **before** the 5 s reboot timeout can fire.

Thermal cut-out is now largely ruled out as the *mechanism* (a firmware thermal shutdown neither blinks
caps lock nor auto-reboots in 18 s). The degraded cooling (idle 70–74 °C) and the 2022 BIOS remain real
second-order problems — they will cause throttling and instability, and the BIOS is implicated in the
`failed to get target temp from SBIOS` errors — but they are no longer the primary explanation.

The 2026-07/08 NVIDIA GSP storms and the recurring `mt7921e` timeout loops remain the leading
**drivers** of the panic. Which one it is will be read directly off the first successful dump.

## Consequence for the plan

The critical path is now **fixing the panic capture**, which is cheap, testable and deterministic:
resize crashkernel → reboot → `kdump-config test` → confirm a vmcore appears. Once that works, the next
natural crash hands over the actual stack trace, and hardware spending can wait until the trace
implicates something.

# Original (superseded) summary — kept for the audit trail

Host `rgardler-AI-Laptop` suffers **recurring total machine freezes**: the machine becomes completely
unresponsive and the **caps-lock LED blinks**. The only recovery has historically been a power-cycle.
Frequency escalated from roughly one per 3–6 weeks (Jun–Sep) to **four reboots in one day** on
2026-10-30 and further crashes on 2026-11-01.

Related background: the network-drop work already done on this host (`mt7921e disable_aspm=1`,
`wifi-watchdog.service`) mitigates a real, separate symptom on the same hardware.

# Crash register (evidence base)

| Boot end | Time | Last-signature | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| -15 | Jul 30 21:30:55 | `NVRM … Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY]` in `kernel_gsp.c:5796` | Died inside NVIDIA storm |
| -14 | Aug 20 13:40:44 | `journald: Under memory pressure, flushing caches` | Unclear |
| -13 | Aug 22 21:24:27 | `NVRM … mmu_walk_unmap.c:62`, `gpu_vaspace.c:4916` | Died inside NVIDIA storm |
| -11 | Sep 21 05:53:37 | tailscaled `panic: ipnlocal: watchdog timeout`, 7 s after last NVRM error | Wedge, then userspace panic |
| -9 | Oct 03 21:49:56 | tailscaled goroutine dump, boot ends | Unclear |
| -8 | Oct 18 06:52:00 | `mt7921e: driver own failed` / `Timeout for driver own` loop | Wi-Fi PCIe wedge |
| -6 | Oct 30 12:28:49 | `mt7921e` timeouts while NetworkManager stopped | Shutdown stall |
| -4 | Oct 30 21:34:28 | tailscaled map long-poll timeout; **18 s to next boot** | **Panic, auto-reboot, no dump** |
| -3 | Oct 30 23:58:53 | `mt7921e: driver own failed` + GNOME/bluetooth re-registration | Panic/wedge, 40 s to next boot |
| -2 | Nov 01 11:29:26 | `mt7921e: Timeout for driver own` | Clean reboot sequence |
| -1 (old) | Nov 01 15:09:45 | None — last entry a routine wifi-watchdog run | **Panic, no dump, 250 s to power-cycle** |
| **-1 (new)** | **Nov 01 19:38:58** | **Deliberate SysRq crash ('c')** | **Reproduced the LED blink; still no dump** |

# Children (remediation work)

1. **Freeze forensics** — fix panic capture (crashkernel sizing, verified by `kdump-config test`),
   telemetry, evidence bundle. **Now the critical path.**
2. Operator runbook — BIOS, thermal service, battery, memtest. Demoted to second-order, still valid.
3. MT7921e isolation experiment — remains valid, and is now cheaper: once dumps work, the trace may
   name the driver directly and make the week-long experiment unnecessary.

# Non-goals

- Re-litigating the network-drop mitigations (`disable_aspm=1`, `wifi-watchdog`) — those stay.
- Buying hardware (battery, thermal paste) before the first real dump is read.
- Removing `kernel.panic=5`, `panic_on_oops=1`, kdump or pstore.

# Assumptions

- The ~2 Hz caps-lock blink observed on the deliberate panics matches the pattern of the unexplained
  crashes; the operator reports it does. This is the load-bearing assumption of the correction and
  should be re-confirmed on the next natural crash (photograph or video the LED).
- The host is ~5–6 years old (BIOS 2022) and its cooling is degraded; idle 70–74 °C is abnormal.

# Goal

As the operator of a host that panics repeatedly, I want every panic to hand over a **readable trace**
automatically, so that each occurrence identifies its own root cause instead of producing another
unanswerable question.

Parent: WL-0MVY88KU8005XFZ4. This is the **critical path** of the epic: it is cheap, deterministic and
self-verifying, and it converts every future crash from an investigation into a read.

# Problem (measured 2026-11-01)

Crashes reach `panic()` — the caps-lock LED shows the Linux panic blink (~1 blink per 0.5 s), reproduced
by a deliberate SysRq crash. Nothing has ever been captured, for four compounding reasons:

```
$ kdump-config show
current state:              ready to kdump
crashkernel addr: 0x                                 <-- empty: no usable crash region
crashkernel suggested size: 1103M

$ cat /etc/default/grub.d/kdump-tools.cfg
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="$GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT crashkernel=2G-4G:320M,4G-32G:512M,32G-64G:1024M,..."

$ cat /sys/kernel/kexec_crash_size
536870912                                            # 512 MB reserved vs 1103 MB needed
```

1. **crashkernel is undersized**: 512 MB reserved against a 1103 MB requirement (kdump initrd is 244 MB
   on disk / 310 MB recorded). The crash kernel cannot boot, so no vmcore is written and the machine
   reboots empty. `current state: ready to kdump` was true and useless — it does not test a dump.
2. **pstore cannot work on this firmware**: `efi_pstore` is loaded, but
   `/sys/firmware/efi/efivars` exposes **no dump variable store**, so there is nothing to persist to.
   kdump is the only viable path; pstore must be recorded as a dead end rather than a fallback.
3. **journald cannot flush at panic**: the journal always stops mid-sentence; panic text goes only to the
   console.
4. **`quiet splash` hides the console**, so even the visible panic was invisible.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC-A — crashkernel resized.** `/etc/default/grub.d/kdump-tools.cfg` reserves at least the size
      `kdump-config show` reports as suggested (allocate **1280M** for margin), and the larger-RAM
      branches are made consistent (32G-64G must not be smaller than 4G-32G). `update-grub` run.
      Verified after reboot: `kexec_crash_size` ≥ 1103 MB, `kdump-config show` prints a **populated**
      `crashkernel addr: 0x…`, and `current state: ready to kdump`.
- [ ] **AC-B — capture proven with a synthetic panic.** `sudo kdump-config test` run with the operator
      present, and a `vmcore` + `dmesg` land in `/var/crash`. Evidence recorded on this item: directory
      listing with sizes and timestamps. **This item does not close until a synthetic panic yields a
      dump** — "ready to kdump" is not proof and has already misled us once.
- [ ] **AC-C — the failed-dump path is observable.** The console is watched during AC-B and what the
      crash kernel prints is recorded on this item. Optionally use `KDUMP_FAIL_CMD` to hold the console
      on failure, so a failed dump leaves a readable trace instead of another blank.
- [ ] **AC-D — `docs/dev/crash-reporting.md` corrected.** Its "kdump is functional / no further action
      required" conclusion is replaced with the measured truth (undersized reservation, no dump ever
      produced, pstore unusable, journald cannot flush, `quiet splash` hides the console), plus a
      "Silent freezes / panic blink" section carrying the parent's corrected observatory table.
- [ ] **AC-E — lockups converted to panics.** `kernel.hardlockup_panic=1` persisted via
      `/etc/sysctl.d/`, with `softlockup_panic` and `hung_task_panic` explicitly considered and the
      decision recorded either way. One documented revert step.
- [ ] **AC-F — interim on-screen capture.** `kernel.panic_print` enabled (e.g. `0x1f` or `0xff`) and the
      console made readable (drop `quiet splash`, or add an explicit `console=`), with a documented
      procedure for the operator to photograph the panic screen. This works even if kdump still fails,
      and costs nothing.
- [ ] **AC-G — telemetry sampler.** A timer-driven (≤10 s) oneshot writes one structured `HOSTWATCH`
      line to journald with: `k10temp`, `acpitz` and MT7921e temperatures, `/proc/loadavg`,
      `MemAvailable`, `wlp3s0` operstate, and any `mt7921e`/`NVRM` error counts since the previous
      sample. No daemon; per-sample at `info`, change-only at `warning`; no `nmcli`/`iw` calls (must not
      perturb the fragile Wi-Fi link).
- [ ] **AC-H — evidence bundle.** `scripts/collect-freeze-evidence.sh` gathers: any vmcore and crash
      dmesg, last N `HOSTWATCH` samples, previous-boot kernel tail, and a classification against the
      crash register (`silent` / `mt7921e-timeout` / `NVRM-storm` / `panic-dump-available`). Emits a
      `SUMMARY.md` whose first line states the classification and confidence. Unit-tested against
      journal fixtures; an unrecognised shape must fail the test, never silently report "unknown".
- [ ] **AC-I — end-to-end verification on this host**: a normal (non-crash) reboot produces a bundle
      showing the clean-shutdown signature, proving the pipeline works before it is needed. Then the
      full suite via the test skill.

# Ordering

AC-A + AC-B first, on their own: ~15 minutes of configuration plus one deliberate reboot, and they turn
every future crash into a read. AC-G/AC-H are conveniences and must not delay A/B.

# Constraints

- No long-running daemon — systemd timer or cron oneshot, following `scripts/install-memwatch.sh`
  (root-owned install path; a timer pointing into a user-writable checkout is a privilege-escalation
  vector).
- Sampler must only read sysfs/procfs.
- kdump, pstore module and `kernel.panic=5` / `panic_on_oops=1` stay enabled.

# Key files (predicted)

- `/etc/default/grub.d/kdump-tools.cfg` (crashkernel sizing; shipped by kdump-tools).
- `/etc/sysctl.d/` snippet for `hardlockup_panic` / `panic_print`.
- `scripts/hostwatch.sh` + `scripts/install-hostwatch.sh`.
- `scripts/collect-freeze-evidence.sh`.
- `tests/test_hostwatch.py`, `tests/test_collect_freeze_evidence.py`.
- `docs/dev/crash-reporting.md` (correction + new section).

# Risks

- **Resizing crashkernel costs ~1.3 GB of usable RAM** on a 30 GB host. Acceptable during the
  investigation; documented so it can be reverted.
- **`kdump-config test` crashes the host on purpose.** Operator present, work saved, self-reboot
  expected.
- **`hardlockup_panic=1` can convert an NMI storm into a reboot loop.** Revert documented.
- **A too-chatty sampler can mask timing-sensitive faults.** Keep the read set minimal and read-only.

# Goal

As the operator, I want a single, ordered, low-risk procedure that takes this host from "freezes with a
blinking caps-lock LED several times a day" to "stable", covering the vendor-facing actions only a
human can perform (BIOS, thermal hardware, battery, memory test), so I can work through it without
re-deriving the diagnosis.

Parent: WL-0MVY88KU8005XFZ4.

# Why this exists

The parent RCA concluded the fault is hardware/firmware level, and that the highest-value actions are
physically performed by the operator, not by software. Those actions are currently undocumented, and
each has a risk (a failed BIOS flash bricks the laptop) or a prerequisite (external display, backup,
downtime window). This item produces the runbook.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/dev/host-freeze-remediation-runbook.md` exists, structured as an **ordered** procedure with
      a clear "do these first" ranking, an expected-time and expected-downtime per step, and a
      **pre-condition / action / verification / rollback** block for each step.
- [ ] The runbook leads with the two free, reversible steps (evidence capture from the sibling item,
      and recording the caps-lock blink code) before any step that requires a reboot or hardware work.
- [ ] **BIOS step** is complete and specific to this machine: identify the current version
      (FA506IE.302, 2022-12-28), how to obtain the correct ASUS package for the FA506IE model
      specifically (the TUF A15 model number must be verified from the DMI string before flashing —
      flashing the wrong variant bricks the unit), the flash method, the mains-power and battery-level
      preconditions, and the recovery path if the flash fails.
- [ ] The runbook explains *why* the BIOS matters here, with this host's own evidence: the boot-time
      `NVRM: … failed to get target temp from SBIOS` and `ACPI BIOS Error (bug): Could not resolve
      symbol [_TZ.THRM._SCP.CTYP]` records, which show the EC/SBIOS thermal handshake is broken on the
      installed firmware.
- [ ] **Thermal service step** documents the measurement that justifies it (idle 70–74 °C: `k10temp`
      70 °C, `acpitz` 74 °C), how to re-measure before and after, what to clean and what to re-paste,
      and the warning that disassembly of a TUF A15 requires care with the battery connector and the
      warranty position.
- [ ] **Battery step** documents the health evidence (2.401 Ah of 4.110 Ah design = 58 %), the test
      that distinguishes a sagging pack from a thermal cut-out (run on AC with the battery
      disconnected for a defined period and compare against the crash register), and the replacement
      criteria.
- [ ] **Memory step** documents an overnight memtest86+ procedure (non-ECC DDR4 produces silent
      corruption with no MCE record), including how to boot it from the Ubuntu GRUB menu and the pass
      count that constitutes a result.
- [ ] A **caps-lock blink observation sheet** is included: exactly what to record (count of blinks per
      group, pause between groups, number of repeats), where to record it, and why it matters (the ASUS
      EC blink code identifies the failing subsystem). This is called out as the single most valuable
      observation available at crash time.
- [ ] The runbook has a **decision table** mapping each observation (blink code, temperature after
      service, memtest result, Ethernet-only experiment outcome) to the next action, so the operator
      does not have to re-interpret results.
- [ ] Every step records the evidence that confirms success, so the parent item can be closed on
      measured stability (e.g. "no freeze for N days with the crash register showing clean shutdowns").
- [ ] Cross-references the sibling items (freeze forensics for evidence capture; MT7921e isolation) and
      `docs/dev/crash-reporting.md`.

# Constraints

- Documentation only — no code, no scripts in this item.
- UK English; `docs/dev/` conventions as used by `rca-*.md` and `snapd-investigation.md`.
- Do not recommend actions that require a purchase without flagging cost/benefit (battery, thermal
  paste) and without giving the free diagnostic that can rule them out first.
- Do not present the BIOS flash as unconditionally safe; the rollback/recovery path is mandatory
  content, and the model-number verification is a hard gate.

# Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/host-freeze-remediation-runbook.md` (new).

# Risks

- **A wrong-model BIOS flash bricks the host.** Mitigated by an explicit model-verification gate using
  `/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name` (`ASUS TUF Gaming A15 FA506IE_FA506IE`) and board revision.
- **The runbook is followed while the machine is unstable**, so a step may be interrupted by a freeze.
  Order steps so that nothing destructive is pending across a power loss.
- **Operator time.** Steps are ranked so the free/reversible ones come first and can be done today.
